title: Regeneration can start without injury, so a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Regeneration can start without injury, so a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because headless planaria mounted a regenerative response with no triggering injury, the authors argue this is consistent with the idea that a missing-tissue response may not be necessary for regeneration and that subtle internal dynamics may suffice to initiate change long after a process seems to have stabilized.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The newly demonstrated ability to mount a regenerative response without any triggering injury is consistent with the idea that a MTR may not be necessary for regeneration to occur [90] and that subtle internal dynamics may be sufficient to initiate change long after the process appears to have reached a stable point.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Discussion”. Scope: Planarian regeneration (Dugesia japonica)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The lack of a contemporaneous external injury is observable, but it cannot by itself decide whether an endogenous missing-tissue response occurred. Existing public molecular data are unlikely to be synchronized to these rare events, leaving only part of the mechanism testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use continuous records to verify that late regeneration begins without a new external wound, then test whether molecular markers defining a missing-tissue response precede the event. Absence of those markers would support MTR-independence; their presence would refute it for these animals.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public expression datasets may not sample the rare late transition.

No external injury does not imply absence of an internal injury-like response.

The missing-tissue response lacks a universally agreed marker set.

analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether a new injury preceded each late regenerative event is decidable from longitudinal notes, and those notes are not public. The aggregate result mixes fission with other morphology changes, so the existing summary does not separate regeneration-without-injury from regeneration-after-a-late-wound. A general claim about the missing-tissue response needs cohorts beyond this experiment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify each late planarian morphology change by whether a new wound, fission, or bite occurred in the preceding interval. Events with no wound would support initiation without a missing-tissue response; restriction of late heads to post-fission wounds would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A possibility claim that a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary is weakly refutable.

The paper's own repatterning classes include fission, which opens a wound, and those classes are not deposited animal by animal.
